title: Reliable matches and a polished table
changes: Jev wins and losses now appear in account statistics and survive detailed game retention. Statistics refresh when opening your account.
Terms acceptance stays saved to your account until the agreement text changes. Account controls have clearer checkboxes, spacing and reliable loading states.
Desktop camera controls sit together near the legal links, with centered icons and spin control. Opponent shots preserve your chosen spin.
Calling the 8-ball pocket has a clear status prompt and larger selection targets. The win celebration has refined sparkles and a centered 8-ball emblem.
Online shot rejection restores authoritative state so players can retry. Concurrent simulation limits are enforced before asynchronous work begins.
Container builds are checked before release, dependencies use committed lockfiles, and unsuccessful deployment health checks fail CI.

title: A gold coin on the table
changes: The opening toss uses a plain gold coin with H and T faces. It flies in from offscreen, flips, and lands on the felt to reveal who breaks.
Reduced motion shows the selected face without the flight animation. Server-selected breakers and resume behavior remain unchanged.
Close-button X icons are centered consistently across panels and the tutorial.

title: Clearer views, account access and winning moments
changes: After cue-ball placement, automatic camera framing can find a clear legal shot lane and show the cue, target and pocket without changing the shot or called pocket.
Signed-in usernames and account settings are visible from the main HUD. The refined mouse/trackpad selector sits above legal controls, and the app is named Pool Simulator.
Completed racks show the winner, a brief reduced-motion-aware confetti celebration and replay actions for local, CPU, Jev and online sessions.

Fixed an airborne jaw collision and added mirrored flight regressions. Tournament off-table objects stay out; the 8 off on the break is spotted with opponent kitchen placement. Bar keeps its house rules.
The tutorial teaches the actual selected interface: mouse/trackpad pull-and-release with the live power bar, or touch power and Shoot controls.
A coin toss chooses the opening player in local, CPU, Jev and online games. Server games keep their chosen breaker on resume.
Human shots against Jev start moving immediately while the server validates and resolves the shot. Delayed results reconcile after playback without a second strike.

title: Welcome flow and guided practice
changes: New visitors get a welcome screen with game context, explicit terms acceptance, a separate optional analytics choice and a prominent quick tutorial option.
The interactive tutorial uses staged offline practice shots and camera framing, with compact instructions that leave the table and current controls usable on phones and desktops.
Tutorial instructions follow touch, mouse or trackpad controls. Exiting practice restores the previous local game.

title: Opponent cue strokes and purposeful cluster shots
changes: CPU and Jev show their selected aim, cue pullback and stroke before the balls move. The human cue stays hidden while the opponent plans, and player shot controls remain locked during opponent turns. Camera controls remain available.
Opponent strokes respect reduced-motion preferences and cancel safely when leaving or restarting a game.
The AI planner considers firmer shots and measured cluster development, balancing useful openings against scratches and opportunities left to the opponent.
Fixed cue aiming changes during pending shots so the visible direction stays aligned with the submitted shot.
Combined camera input mode, camera actions and contextual hints into a compact HUD panel.

title: Trackpad camera controls and keyboard flight
changes: Added a visible desktop Mouse & Keyboard Mode / Trackpad Mode selector that remembers your preference. Trackpad mode uses two-finger scrolling to orbit, pinch to zoom and Option/Alt-scroll to pan.
Expanded camera flight: WASD moves across the table, Space rises, Left Shift descends and Q/E turns. Enter takes a quick shot only when the table has keyboard focus; Space no longer shoots.
Camera gestures cancel pending shot pulls and protect cue aim while you adjust your view. Visible camera controls provide alternatives to gestures.

title: Tactical AI planning and reliable ball placement
changes: Jev now chooses tactical shots using previews from the real game physics, including direct pots, banks, kicks, combinations and safeties. Plans consider cue position, continuation and opponent replies.
Fixed CPU and Jev ball-in-hand planning so they place the cue and execute a shot together. Head-string shots can plan a legal cushion escape before returning to a ball in the kitchen.
The offline CPU now tests a bounded set of shots before playing, instead of falling back to a break shot when direct pots are unavailable.
Jev records reported token usage even when a model answer is invalid and a local fallback is used. Shot status identifies model choices and local plans.

title: Owner dashboard and movable camera controls
changes: Added a private owner dashboard for searching accounts, managing Premium, and inspecting recorded Jev usage and estimated costs. Owner access is checked on the server and Premium changes are audited.
Settings, View and Online panels can be dragged, moved with buttons or keyboard controls, and reset to their original positions.
Added WASD camera movement and a compact HUD camera pad for touch devices.

title: Premium accounts and unlimited Jev games
changes: Premium accounts have a badge in Settings and Account, with unlimited Jev games and no midnight expiry.
While playing Jev with Premium, New rack starts another server-owned game. Selecting Jev resumes your active game.
Added an operator command to enable or disable Premium. Existing accounts and game records are preserved during the database upgrade.

title: Daily Jev AI games and privacy controls
changes: Added Jev AI alongside the offline CPU. Signed-in adults can start or resume one free Jev game per account and network per UTC day, with server-owned turns and physics.
Added private per-game provider token counts and estimated costs, durable daily game limits, and visible CPU fallback for provider outages or capacity limits.
Added Terms and Privacy notices, explicit adult account/Terms acceptance, and independent opt-in analytics with easy withdrawal and GPC/DNT support.
Optional first-party feature sessions are disabled by default and have no public reporting API. Scheduled retention removes old session events and detailed Jev game records.
Jev credentials remain backend-only. Daily-game revisions reject replayed turns, and the production proxy now replaces untrusted client-IP forwarding headers.
Removed the floating mobile Show balls button; tap either compact scorecard to expand or collapse ball details.

Added an optional interactive Help tutorial for aiming, spin, camera movement and shooting, with action feedback, skippable steps and easy dismissal. The tutorial is centered between scorecards and shot controls.

title: CPU opponent terminology
changes: Standardized the computer opponent name as CPU throughout controls, player cards, turn and result messages, account notes, and documentation. Opponent behavior is unchanged.

title: Safer online play
changes: Removed legacy score and replay endpoints, their unused database models, and the obsolete frontend REST transport. Unknown API reads now return 404 instead of a successful SPA fallback.
Added strict WebSocket field validation, message throttles, connection caps, bounded simulation concurrency, and HTTP request-size limits.
Leaving or losing connection after the first shot counts as a casual forfeit. Production shutdowns and server failures remain interruptions without a fabricated winner.
Account stats explicitly describe unranked casual play; private and custom matches do not establish a competitive rating.
Added browser security headers and HTTPS-only HSTS responses. Production WebSockets now enforce smaller transport queues and message limits.
Mobile spin adjustment and Reset stay visible beside the shot controls; More only collapses secondary actions such as CPU and New rack.

title: Room to play on mobile
changes: Touch and drag to aim continuously, then choose power and tap Shoot. Lifting your aiming finger no longer fires accidentally.
Mobile keeps compact player scores visible, with ball details available on demand and secondary shot controls under More.
Use two fingers together to orbit during play and pinch to zoom in the same gesture. Camera mode still offers one-finger orbit and two-finger panning. Trackpads can use Shift-scroll to orbit.
Placement outlines, cue placement rings, head strings, and pocket-call markers now use a contrasting tint of the chosen felt, with dark guides on light cloth.
Dependabot groups frontend and backend runtime and development updates separately, plus Docker images and GitHub Actions, targeting develop for testing before release.

title: Play together, with or without an account
changes: Create a private room and share its invite link. Friends can join as guests with no account required.

Optional accounts have case-insensitive usernames, secure password hashing, cookie sessions, and a one-use recovery code shown when created. Password recovery issues a new code and revokes existing sessions.

Your account shows lifetime online stats and recent matches recorded by the server, with durable match history for future lobby and matchmaking features. Local practice and CPU games remain untracked.
Online results no longer wait for client acknowledgement. Account identities are verified by the server, and disconnected rooms close cleanly without awarding fabricated wins.

Accounts, sessions, and match history persist in the existing SQLite Docker volume. Added authentication limits, request-origin checks, and protection against serving files outside the frontend directory.

title: A natural stance and clearer Bar play
changes: Settings now has a fixed title bar and close button that stay visible while scrolling, with Escape dismissal and keyboard focus restored to the Table button.
Automatic framing uses a lower, closer playing view and tighter bounds around the visible balls. Cue alignment remains adjustable and never overrides a shot being pulled.
Automatic camera framing now swings behind the cue toward the majority of the current player’s legal targets, including the final 8-Ball, with the idle cue facing forward from the new view.

Bar house rules now keep the layout after an empty break instead of automatically reracking. Players alternate until a legal pot assigns groups; pots made with a scratch stay down without assigning a group.
Turn, foul, and result messages use the CPU opponent’s name consistently. Illegal-break reracks now explain the missing pocket and four-rail requirement.
Once groups are assigned, player cards show the 8-Ball after their group, highlighted when it becomes the final target.
Desktop tables open from behind the cue, looking toward the fresh rack.
Pocketed balls visibly fall into deeper pocket wells before entering the return, while scoring updates immediately.
Release history now includes earlier versions reconstructed from repository history.

title: A better view of the table
changes: New camera controls: enter Move camera mode to orbit with one finger and pinch or pan with two. Focus balls, Whole table, and zoom buttons make adjusting the view easier.
Optional automatic framing follows the remaining balls after a shot settles. Enabled by default on mobile, disabled on desktop; manual camera movement takes priority.
Click the version badge to read this release history.
Warmer lighting, shadows, detailed felt and wood, improved cushions and pockets, table legs, and a visible ball return.
Improved cue geometry and assisted elevation, collision handling, and rolling behavior. Optional fast-forward for fine movements.
Clearer player cards and adaptive instructions, immediate pocket indicators, configurable rail sights and cue ball markings, and a spin reset button.
Bar 8-Ball placement guidance and persistent tutorial dismissal. Browser tests run separately from required deployment checks.

title: Playable 8-Ball, online rooms, and a CPU opponent
changes: Added a playable 3D pool table with racked balls, aiming, shot power, spin, cue ball placement, and 8-Ball rules for turns, fouls, and winning.
Added online rooms with join codes and synchronized shots, plus an optional CPU opponent. Fixed the CPU getting stuck before taking its turn.
Added player scorecards, a compact lobby, felt and wood color settings, and desktop camera orbit with right-drag.
Refined pull-back shot controls, softened the power curve for gentler shots, previewed legal cue ball placement, and made aiming independent of frame rate.
Improved pocket capture and jaw geometry, cushion rebounds, spin and collision behavior, and visible ball rolling. Break shots can use more power than regular shots.
Added game sound effects and an installable web app with offline asset caching.

title: Correct version display in deployed builds
changes: Fixed the version badge by including the version information in deployed builds and correcting where the server reads it.

title: Initial application foundation
changes: Established the browser canvas and backend foundation for the pool simulator; playable pool arrived in a later release.
Added the site version badge and the initial deployment setup.
